children.text: upanayanaṃ vyākhyāsyāmaḥ
children.translated_text: We shall explain the upanayana.

children.text: sa purastādeva saṃbhārānupakalpayate pālāśamidhmaṃ khādiramaudumbaraṃ vaikaṅkataṃ vaitadvṛkṣīyām eva darvīṃ karoti tvagbilāṃ mūladaṇḍāratnīṃ caturaṅgulaṃ bilaṃ karoti
children.translated_text: Beforehand he prepares the materials: fuel-sticks of palāśa, khadira, udumbara, or vaikaṅkata wood; he makes the ladle only from such a tree, with its bark as the hollow and its root as the handle, an aratni long, and he makes the hollow four fingers wide.

children.text: sādayācārikaṃ karmeti vijñāyate
children.translated_text: It is understood that the rite is one accompanied by inherited custom.

children.text: garbhāṣṭameṣu brāhmaṇamupanayīta garbhaikādaśeṣu rājanyaṃ garbhadvādaśeṣu vaiśyaṃ garbhanavameṣu brāhmaṇamityaparaṃ vāsāṃsi samāmanantyaiṇeyaṃ brāhmaṇo vasīta rauravaṃ rājanyo bastājinaṃ vaiśyo yadajinaṃ dhārayed brahmavarcavṛdvāso dhārayetkṣatraṃ vardhayedubhayaṃ dhāryamubhayorvṛddhyā iti vijñāyate vasante brāhmaṇamupanayīta grīṣme hemante vā rājanyaṃ śaradi vaiśyaṃ varṣāsu rathakāraṃ śiśire vā sarvānāpūryamāṇapakṣe puṇye nakṣatre viśeṣeṇa puṃnāmadheya āśitasya kumārasya keśānvāpayitvā snātamalaṃkṛtamahataṃ vāsaḥ paridhāpya prācīnapravaṇa udīcīnapravaṇe same vā deśe sthaṇḍilamuddhatyāvokṣyāgniṃ mathitvā laukikaṃ vāhṛtya nyupyopasamādadhāti ||
children.translated_text: He should initiate a brāhmaṇa in the eighth year from conception, a rājanya in the eleventh from conception, and a vaiśya in the twelfth from conception; another opinion says a brāhmaṇa in the ninth from conception. They prescribe garments: a brāhmaṇa should wear an antelope skin, a rājanya a ruru-deer skin, and a vaiśya a goat skin. If he wears a skin, it increases brahmic radiance; if he wears a garment, it increases kṣatra-power; both are to be worn for the increase of both, so it is understood. He should initiate a brāhmaṇa in spring, a rājanya in summer or winter, a vaiśya in autumn, a chariot-maker in the rainy season, or all in the cold season, in the waxing fortnight, under an auspicious nakṣatra, especially one bearing a male name. After the boy has eaten, he has his hair shaved, bathes him, adorns him, clothes him in an unworn garment, then in a place sloping eastward, sloping northward, or level, he raises and sprinkles a ritual ground, kindles fire by friction or brings ordinary fire, places it down, and sets it in order.

children.text: prāgagrairdarbhairagniṃ paristṛṇātyapi vodagagrāḥ paścātpurastācca bhavanti dakṣiṇaḥ pakṣa upariṣṭādbhavatyadhastāduttaro dakṣiṇenāgniṃ brahmāyatane darbhānsaṃstīrya mayi gṛhṇāmyagre agnimiti dvābhyāmātmanyagniṃ dhyātvottareṇāgniṃ pātrebhyaḥ saṃstīrya yathārthaṃ dravyāṇi prayunaktyaśmānamahataṃ vāso 'jinaṃ mauñjīṃ mekhalāṃ trivṛtaṃ brāhmaṇasya maurvīṃ rājanyasya sautrīṃ vaiśyasya bailvaṃ pālāśaṃ vā daṇḍaṃ brāhmaṇasya naiyagrodhaṃ rājanyasyaudumbaraṃ vaiśyasyaikaviṃśatidārumidhmaṃ saṃnahyatyāhutiparimāṇaṃ vā tasmiñchamyāḥ paridhīn upasaṃnahyati darvīṃ kūrcamājyasthālīṃ praṇītāpraṇayanaṃ prokṣaṇīpātramupaveṣaṃ yena cārthaḥ sakṛdeva sarvāṇi yathopapādaṃ vaitasminkāle brahmā yajñopavītaṃ kṛtvāpa ācamyāpareṇāgnimatikramya dakṣiṇato brahmāyatanāttṛṇaṃ nirasyāpa upaspṛśyāgnimabhimukha upaviśatyapareṇāgniṃ prāṅmukha upaviśya samāvaprachinnāgrau darbhau prādeśamātrau pavitre kṛtvānyena nakhāc chittvādbhir anumṛjya ||
children.translated_text: He strews darbha grass around the fire with the tips toward the east, or else the western and eastern sides have tips toward the north; the southern side is above and the northern below. South of the fire, at the seat of the Brahman priest, he spreads darbha grass; with the two verses beginning 'In myself I take Agni first,' he meditates on the fire within himself. North of the fire he spreads grass for the vessels and arranges the substances as needed: a stone, an unworn garment, a skin, a triple muñja girdle for a brāhmaṇa, one of bowstring fiber for a rājanya, one of thread for a vaiśya, a staff of bilva or palāśa for a brāhmaṇa, of nyagrodha for a rājanya, and of udumbara for a vaiśya. He ties together twenty-one fuel-sticks, or enough for the oblations, and in that bundle he ties up the śamyā sticks as enclosing sticks, the ladle, the brush, the ghee-bowl, the vessel for leading the praṇītā water, the sprinkling vessel, the upaveṣa implement, and whatever else is required, all at once and as available. Or, at that time, the Brahman priest, having put on the sacred thread and sipped water, passes behind the fire, removes a blade of grass south of the Brahman's seat, touches water, and sits facing the fire. Sitting west of the fire and facing east, he makes two darbhas with unbroken tips, each a span long, into pavitras, cuts them off with something other than his fingernail, and wipes them with water.

children.text: pavitrāntarhite pātre 'pa ānīyopabilaṃ pātraṃ pūrayitvodagagrābhyāṃ pavitrābhyāṃ trirutpūya samaṃ prāṇairdhārayamāṇo 'viṣiñcan haratyuttareṇāgniṃ praṇītāḥ sādayitvā darbhairapidadhāti praṇītāvatprokṣaṇīḥ saṃskṛtya bilavantyuttānāni kṛtvā viṣāyedhmaṃ triḥ sarvābhiḥ prokṣati darvīṃ niṣṭapya saṃmṛjya punar niṣṭapya nidadhāti saṃmārgānabhyukṣyāgnāvādadhāti pavitrāntarhitāyām ājyasthālyām ājyaṃ nirupyottareṇāgnimaṅgārānnirūhya teṣvadhiśrityāvadyotya darbhataruṇābhyāṃ pratyasya triḥ paryagni kṛtvodagudvāsyāṅgārān pratyūhyodagagrābhyāṃ pavitrābhyāṃ punarāhāraṃ trirutpūya pavitre agnāvādhāya śamyābhiḥ paridadhātyapareṇāgnim udīcīnakumbāṃ śamyāṃ nidadhāti saṃspṛṣṭe madhyamayā prācīnakumbe dakṣiṇāmuttarāṃ cāpareṇāgnim udagagraṃ kūrcaṃ nidhāya tasminprāṅmukha upaviśati yajñopavītaṃ kṛtvāpa ācamya dakṣiṇataḥ kumāra upaviśyānvārabhate ||
children.translated_text: He brings water into a vessel screened by the pavitras, fills the vessel up to the rim, purifies it three times with the two pavitras whose tips point north, and, holding it level with his breaths without spilling, carries it north of the fire. Having set down the praṇītā waters, he covers them with darbhas. He prepares the sprinkling waters like the praṇītā waters, turns the hollowed vessels upright, separates the fuel, and sprinkles everything three times with all the waters. He heats the ladle, wipes it, heats it again, and sets it down; after sprinkling the wipers, he places them on the fire. In the ghee-bowl screened by pavitras he pours ghee, draws coals north of the fire, places it on them, illuminates it, stirs it back with two young darbha shoots, carries it three times around the fire, removes it northward, pushes the coals back, purifies the fresh supply three times with the two pavitras whose tips point north, places the pavitras on the fire, and encloses the fire with śamyā sticks. West of the fire he lays a śamyā stick with its hollow to the north; when it touches the middle one, he lays the southern and northern sticks with their hollows to the east. West of the fire he lays the brush with its tip to the north, and on it he sits facing east. Having put on the sacred thread and sipped water, the boy sits to the south and touches him from behind.

children.text: atha pariṣiñcatyadite 'numanyasveti dakṣiṇato 'numate 'numanyasveti paścātsarasvate 'numanyasvetyuttarato deva savitaḥ prasuveti samantamevaṃ hutvā pariṣiñcati kṛtavanmantrānnamatīdhmaṃ tredhābhyajya sakṛdevādadhātyayaṃ ta idhma ātmā jātavedastena vardhasva cenddhi vardhaya cāsmānprajayā paśubhirbrahmavarcasenānnādyena samedhaya svāhetyuttaraṃ paridhisaṃdhimanvavahṛtya darvīṃ dakṣiṇāprāñcamāsīnaḥ saṃtatamṛjumāghāramāghārayati prajāpatiṃ manasā dhyāyanna ca svāhā karoti dakṣiṇaṃ paridhisaṃdhimanvavahṛtyendrāya svāheti prāñcamudañcaṃ saṃtatamṛjumāghāramāghāryājyabhāgau juhotyagnaye medhapataye svāhetyuttarārdhapūrvārdhe somāya medhapataye svāheti dakṣiṇārdhapūrvārdhe tāvantareṇetarā āhutīrjuhoti sarvadarvihomāṇāmeṣa kalpo mantrānte nityaḥ svāhākāro 'mantrāsvamuṣmai svāheti yathādevatamādiṣṭadevate 'thānādiṣṭadevate 'gnaye svāhā somāya svāhā prajāpataye svāhā viśvebhyo devebhyaḥ svāhāgnaye sviṣṭakṛte svāheti vyāhṛtībhirjuhotyekaikaśaḥ samastābhiśca ||
children.translated_text: Then he sprinkles around with, "<s>Aditi</s>, give permission," on the south; "<s>Anumati</s>, give permission," on the west; "<s>Sarasvatī</s>, give permission," on the north; and "God <s>Savitṛ</s>, impel," all around. Having offered in this way, he sprinkles around. Bowing to the mantras already recited, he smears the fuel threefold with ghee and places it on only once, saying, "This fuel is your self, <s>Jātavedas</s>; by it grow, and kindle, and make us grow with offspring, cattle, brahmanical splendor, and food. Svāhā." Having brought the ladle along the northern junction of the enclosing sticks, seated facing south-east, he pours a continuous straight stream of ghee, meditating in his mind on <s>Prajāpati</s>, and he does not utter svāhā. Having brought it along the southern junction of the enclosing sticks, with "To <s>Indra</s>, svāhā," he pours a continuous straight stream of ghee eastward and northward. He offers the two shares of ghee: "To <s>Agni</s>, lord of wisdom, svāhā," in the northern half of the eastern half; "To <s>Soma</s>, lord of wisdom, svāhā," in the southern half of the eastern half. Between those he offers the other oblations. This is the rule for all ladle-offerings: at the end of a mantra there is always the utterance svāhā; where there are no mantras, "To so-and-so, svāhā," according to the deity. When a deity is specified, to the specified deity; when no deity is specified, "To <s>Agni</s>, svāhā; to <s>Soma</s>, svāhā; to <s>Prajāpati</s>, svāhā; to all the gods, svāhā; to <s>Agni</s> <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s>, svāhā." He offers with the vyāhṛtis, each separately and also with all together.

children.text: tata etā āhutīrjuhoti yā tiraścī nipadyase 'haṃ vidharaṇī iti
children.translated_text: After that he offers these oblations: "You who lie crosswise; I am the supporter."

children.text: tāṃ tvā ghṛtasya dhārayā juhomi vaiśvakarmaṇīṃ svāhā
children.translated_text: "I offer you, the <s>Vaiśvakarmaṇī</s>, with a stream of ghee. Svāhā."

children.text: yānūcī nipadyase 'haṃ saṃrādhanī iti
children.translated_text: "You who lie lengthwise; I am the accomplisher."

children.text: tāṃ tvā ghṛtasya dhārayāgnau saṃrādhanīṃ yaje svāhā
children.translated_text: "I worship you, the accomplisher, in the fire with a stream of ghee. Svāhā."

children.text: saṃrādhanyai devyai svāhā
children.translated_text: "To the goddess Accomplisher, svāhā."

children.text: prasādhanyai devyai svāhā
children.translated_text: "To the goddess Perfecter, svāhā."

children.text: sadasaspatimadbhutaṃ priyamindrasya kāmyam
children.translated_text: "The wondrous lord of the seat, dear to <s>Indra</s>, desirable,"

children.text: saniṃ medhāmayāsiṣaṃ svāhā
children.translated_text: "I seek to obtain as a gain rich in wisdom. Svāhā."

children.text: yukto vaha jātavedaḥ purastādagne viddhi karma kriyamāṇaṃ yathedam
children.translated_text: "Harnessed, carry it, <s>Jātavedas</s>; in front, O <s>Agni</s>, know this rite that is being performed."

children.text: tvaṃ bhiṣagbheṣajasyāsi kartā tvayā gā aśvānpuruṣānsanema svāhā
children.translated_text: "You are the physician, the maker of the remedy; through you may we win cows, horses, and men. Svāhā."

children.text: āyurdā deva jarasaṃ gṛṇāno ghṛtapratīko ghṛtapṛṣṭho agne
children.translated_text: "O god <s>Agni</s>, giver of life, praised for old age, with ghee as your face and ghee on your back,"

children.text: ghṛtaṃ pibannamṛtaṃ cāru gavyaṃ piteva putraṃ jarase nayemaṃ svāhetyatha vāsaso 'ntānsaṃmārṣṭi yā akṛntannavayanyā atanvata yāśca devīrantānabhito 'dadanta
children.translated_text: "drinking ghee, immortal, lovely, bovine, may we lead this one to old age as a father leads a son. Svāhā." Then he wipes the ends of the garment: "Those goddesses who cut, who wove, who stretched out, and who set the ends on both sides,"

children.text: tāstvā devīrjarase saṃvyayantvāyuṣmānidaṃ paridhatsva vāsa ityathainaṃ paridhāpayati paridhatta dhatta vāsasainaṃ śatāyuṣaṃ kṛṇuta dīrghamāyuḥ
children.translated_text: "may those goddesses wrap you for old age. Put on this garment, endowed with life." Then he makes him put it on: "Clothe him; place the garment on him; make him one who lives a hundred years, with long life."

children.text: bṛhaspatiḥ prāyacchadvāsa etatsomāya rājñe paridhātavā u
children.translated_text: "<s>Bṛhaspati</s> gave this garment to king <s>Soma</s> to put on."

children.text: jarāṃ gacchāsi paridhatsva vāso bhavā kṛṣṭīṇāmabhiśastipāvā
children.translated_text: "You shall reach old age; put on the garment. Become one who removes curses among peoples."

children.text: śataṃ ca jīva śaradaḥ suvarcā rāyaśca poṣamupasaṃvyayasveti ||
children.translated_text: "Live a hundred autumns, bright in splendor, and wrap yourself in wealth and prosperity."

children.text: parihitamabhimantrayate parīdaṃ vāso adhidhāḥ svastaye 'bhūrāpīnāmabhiśastipāvā
children.translated_text: When it has been put on, he addresses it with a mantra: "You have wrapped this garment around for well-being; you have become one who protects kinsmen from curses."

children.text: śataṃ ca jīva śaradaḥ purūcīrvasūni cāryo vibhajāsi jīvannityathāsya prathamavāsyamādatte yasya te prathamavāsyaṃ harāmastaṃ tvā viśve avantu devāḥ
children.translated_text: "Live a hundred numerous autumns; while living, distribute goods to the worthy." Then he takes his first-worn garment, saying, "We take away your first-worn garment. May all the gods protect you."

children.text: taṃ vā bhrātaraḥ suhṛdo vardhamānamanujāyantāṃ bahavaḥ sujātamityathainaṃ mauñjyā mekhalayā trivṛtā madhyataḥ saṃnahyati yā bṛhatī duritā rarāṇā śarma varūthaṃ punatī na āgāt
children.translated_text: "May many brothers and friends be born after you as you grow, well-born." Then he girds him around the middle with a threefold girdle of muñja grass: "This girdle, broad, warding off evils, has come to us, purifying shelter and protection."

children.text: prāṇāpānābhyāṃ balamābharantī svasā devānāṃ subhagā mekhaleyamiti granthiṃ grathnāti prāṇānāṃ granthirasi sa mā visrasa ityathājinamuttaraṃ paridhatte mitrasya cakṣurdharuṇaṃ balīyastejo yaśasvi sthaviraṃ samiddham
children.translated_text: "Bringing strength through the in-breath and out-breath, this fortunate girdle, sister of the gods." He ties the knot: "You are the knot of the vital breaths; do not slip away from me." Then he puts the antelope skin on him above: "The eye of <s>Mitra</s>, a support, stronger, radiant, glorious, firm, kindled,"

children.text: anāhanasyaṃ vasanaṃ jariṣṇu parīdaṃ vājyajinaṃ dadhe 'hamiti jayābhyātānānnāṣṭrabhṛta iti hutvaitā āhutīrjuhoti pūrṇā paścādimaṃ me varuna tattvā yāmi tvaṃ no 'gne sa tvaṃ no agne tvamagne 'yāsyayāścāgne 'syanabhiśastīśca yadasya karmaṇo 'tyarīricaṃ prajāpata ityuttamāṃ hutvā gurave varaṃ dadāti ||
children.translated_text: "unassailable clothing, enduring: I put on this powerful antelope skin." Having offered the <s>Jayā</s>, <s>Abhyātāna</s>, and <s>Rāṣṭrabhṛt</s> oblations, he offers these oblations: <s>Pūrṇā</s>, <s>Paścāt</s>, "This of mine, O <s>Varuṇa</s>," "I go to that truth of yours," "You, O <s>Agni</s>, are ours," "So you, O <s>Agni</s>, are ours," "You, O <s>Agni</s>, are the expeller," "And those curses, O <s>Agni</s>," and "What of this rite has gone beyond measure, O <s>Prajāpati</s>." Having offered the last, he gives a boon-fee to the teacher.

children.text: apareṇāgniṃ dvayāndarbhānpūrvāparānudagagrānstṛṇāti teṣu pūrvāparāvupatiṣṭhete prāṅmukhaḥ pratyaṅmukhasya hastaṃ gṛhṇīyādityekaṃ pratyaṅmukhaḥ prāṅmukhasyetyaparamathainayoḥ praiṣakṛdañjalī udakena pūrayatyathāsyāñjalināñjalāvadukamānayati śaṃ no devīrabhiṣṭaya āpo bhavantu pītaye
children.translated_text: To the west of the fire he spreads two sets of darbha grass, running east-west, with their tips to the north. On them the two stand, one to the east and the other to the west. Facing east, one should take the hand of the one facing west, according to one rule; facing west, that of the one facing east, according to the other. Then the prompter fills their joined hands with water. Then with his joined hands he pours water into their joined hands, saying, "May the divine waters be auspicious for us, for help; may they be fit for drinking."

children.text: śaṃ yorabhisravantu na ityathāsya dakṣiṇena hastena dakṣiṇaṃ hastamabhīvāṅguṣṭhamabhīva lomāni gṛhṇāti devasya tvā savituḥ prasave 'śvinorbāhubhyāṃ pūṣṇo hastābhyāṃ hastena te hastaṃ gṛhṇāmi savitrā prasūtaḥ ko nāmāsītyasāvitītaraḥ pratyāha tasya nāmābhipadya japatyasau savitā te hastamagrabhīdagniṣṭa ācāryaḥ kasya brahmacāryasi kasmai tvā kāya tvā kamupanayāmyāgantā mā riṣeṇyataḥ prasthāvāno bhāvasthātu samanyavo dṛḍhāścidamariṣṇavaḥ kṛśāścidamariṣṇava ā ganta saṃrabhāvahai preto mṛtyuṃ nudāvahai na mṛtyuścaratīha ||
children.translated_text: "Let the auspicious streams flow for both of us; not..." Then, with his right hand, he grasps the boy's right hand, including the thumb and including the hairs, saying, "At the impulse of the god <s>Savitṛ</s>, with the arms of the <s>Aśvins</s>, with the hands of <s>Pūṣan</s>, I grasp your hand with my hand, impelled by <s>Savitṛ</s>. What is your name?" The other replies, "I am so-and-so." Pronouncing his name, he mutters, "So-and-so, <s>Savitṛ</s> has grasped your hand. <s>Agni</s> is your teacher. Whose brahmacārin are you? For whom, to whom, and unto what do I initiate you? Come here. Do not be harmed from here. Be setting forth, be standing, of one mind. Even the strong should be unharmed; even the weak should be unharmed. Come; let us take hold together. Come forth; let us drive away death. Death does not move here."

children.text: prāṇāya tvācāryāya paridadāmi kuberāya tvā mahārājāya paridadāmi takṣakāya tvā vaiśāleyāya paridadāmyagnaye tvā paridadāmi vāyave tvā paridadāmi sūryāya tvā paridadāmi prajāpataye tvā paridadāmi prajāpata imaṃ gopāyāmumiti paridāyāthāsya dakṣiṇamaṃsaṃ prati bāhumanvavahṛtya nābhideśamabhimṛśati yuvā suvāsāḥ parivīta āgātsa u śreyānbhavati jāyamānaḥ
children.translated_text: "I hand you over to breath and to the teacher. I hand you over to <s>Kubera</s>, the great king. I hand you over to <s>Takṣaka Vaiśāleya</s>. I hand you over to <s>Agni</s>. I hand you over to <s>Vāyu</s>. I hand you over to <s>Sūrya</s>. I hand you over to <s>Prajāpati</s>. <s>Prajāpati</s>, guard this one, so-and-so." Having thus handed him over, he then brings his arm down along the boy's right shoulder and touches the region of the navel, saying, "A youth, well clothed and invested, has come. He becomes more excellent as he is being born.

children.text: taṃ dhīrāsaḥ kavaya annayanti svādhiyo manasā devayanta ityathāsya dakṣiṇaṃ karṇamājapati bhūstvayi dadhāmi bhuvastvayi dadhāmītyuttaraṃ suvastvayi dadhāmīti dakṣiṇamapi vottarameva dviḥ sakṛdeva dakṣiṇamathainamaśmānamāsthāpayatyātiṣṭhemamaśmānamaśmeva tvaṃ sthiro bhava pramṛṇīhi durasyūnsahasva pṛtanyata iti tataḥ samidhamādhāpayatyagnaye samidhamāhāriṣaṃ bṛhate jātavedase yathā tvamagne samidhā samidhyasa evaṃ māmāyuṣā varcasā sanyā medhayā prajayā paśubhirbrahmavarcasenānnādyena samedhaya svāhetyekāmādadhāti tisra eke saptaike pradakṣiṇamagniṃ parikramya dakṣiṇata udagāvṛtyopaviśyopasaṃgṛhya pṛcchati ||
children.translated_text: The wise, the inspired poets, lead him on, desiring the gods with good thoughts in their minds." Then he murmurs into his right ear, "I place <s>bhūḥ</s> in you; I place <s>bhuvaḥ</s> in you," into the left, "I place <s>suvaḥ</s> in you," into the right; or else into the left twice and into the right only once. Then he makes him stand on a stone, saying, "Stand upon this stone; like a stone be firm. Crush those who wish evil; overpower those who attack." children.translated_text: Then her brother, with joined hands, puts parched grain, spread below and sprinkled with ghee, into her joined hands. This woman speaks as she offers the parched grain into the fire:

children.text: dīrghāyurastu me patiredhantāṃ jñātayo mama
children.translated_text: "May my husband have long life; may my kinsmen prosper.

children.text: bhagena tvā saṃsṛjāmi māsareṇa surāmivetyathaināṃ vācayatīmānlājānāvapāmi samṛddhikaraṇānmama
children.translated_text: I join you with <s>Bhaga</s>, like liquor with its ferment." Then he makes her recite: "I offer these parched grains, makers of prosperity, for myself

children.text: tubhyaṃ ca saṃvananāṃstadagniranumanyatāmiyaṃ svāhetyevameva trirāsthāpayati triḥ pariṇayati trirāvapatyathaināṃ prācīṃ vodīcīṃ vā ||
children.translated_text: and for union with you; may <s>Agni</s> consent to this woman. Svāhā." In just this way he makes her step upon the stone three times, leads her around three times, and has her offer three times. Then he makes her advance eastward or northward.

children.text: sapta padāni prakramayatyekamiṣe viṣṇustvānvetu dve ūrje viṣṇustvānvetu trīṇi vratāya viṣṇustvānvetu catvāri māyobhavāya viṣṇustvānvetu pañca paśubhyo viṣṇustvānvetu ṣaḍrāyaspoṣāya viṣṇustvānvetu sapta saptabhyo hotrābhyo viṣṇustvānvetviti saptame pade samīkṣamāṇo japati sakhā saptapadā bhava sakhāyau saptapadāvabhūva
children.translated_text: He makes her take seven steps: "For one step, may <s>Viṣṇu</s> follow you for food. For two, may <s>Viṣṇu</s> follow you for strength. For three, may <s>Viṣṇu</s> follow you for vows. For four, may <s>Viṣṇu</s> follow you for well-being. For five, may <s>Viṣṇu</s> follow you for cattle. For six, may <s>Viṣṇu</s> follow you for wealth and nourishment. For seven, may <s>Viṣṇu</s> follow you for the seven priestly offices." At the seventh step, looking at her, he murmurs: "Be a friend through seven steps. We two have become friends through seven steps.

children.text: sakhyaṃ te gameyaṃ sakhyātte mā yoṣaṃ sakhyānme mā yoṣṭhā ityathāsyā dakṣiṇamaṃsaṃ prati bāhumanvavahṛtya hṛdayadeśamabhimṛśati mama hṛdaye hṛdayaṃ te astu mama citte cittamastu te
children.translated_text: May I attain friendship with you; may I not be separated from your friendship; may you not be separated from my friendship." Then, passing his arm behind her toward her right shoulder, he touches the region of her heart: "Let your heart be in my heart; let your mind be in my mind.

children.text: mama vācamekamanā śṛṇu māmevānuvratā bhava sahacaryā mayā bhavetyathāsyā dakṣiṇaṃ karṇamājapati ||
children.translated_text: Listen to my speech with one mind. Be devoted to me alone. Be my companion." Then he murmurs into her right ear.

children.text: athāsyāḥ svadhitiṃ mūrdhni dhārayanhiraṇyaṃ vodakumbhenāvasiñcatyāpo hi ṣṭhā mayobhuva iti tisṛbhirhiraṇyavarṇāḥ śucayaḥ pāvakā iti catasṛbhiḥ pavamānaḥ suvarjana ityetenānuvākenāvasicya yathārthaṃ vahantyuhyamānāmanumantrayate ye vadhvaścandraṃ vahatuṃ yakṣmā yanti janāmanu
children.translated_text: Then, holding an axe on her head, he sprinkles her with gold or with a water-pot, with the three verses beginning "For you are waters bringing bliss," with the four beginning "Golden-colored, pure, purifying," and, after sprinkling her with this anuvāka, "The purifier, winning heaven," they carry her as appropriate. As she is being carried, he addresses her with a mantra: "The consumptions of the bride that go with the bridal train among people,

children.text: punastānyajñiyā devā nayantu yata āgatā ityathaināṃ gṛhānuhyānaḍuhe rohite carmaṇyupaveśayatīha gāvo niṣīdantvihāśvā iha puruṣāḥ
children.translated_text: may the sacrificial gods lead them back to where they came from." Then, having brought her to the house, he seats her on the hide of a red bull: "Here may the cows sit down; here the horses; here the men.

children.text: iho sahasradakṣiṇo 'bhi pūṣā niṣīdatvityathaināmāgneyena sthālīpākena yājayatyathaitasya sthālīpākasyopahatyābhighārya juhotyagnaye svāhāgnaye 'gnivate svāhāgnaye 'nnādāya svāhāgnaye sviṣṭakṛte svāheti yāvajjīvametamagniṃ vrīhibhiryavairvā sāyaṃ prātaḥ paricaratyagnaye svāheti sāyaṃ pūrvāmāhutiṃ juhoti prajāpataye svāhetyuttarāṃ saurīṃ pūrvāṃ prātareke samāmanantyaupāsano nityo dhāryo 'nugato manthyaḥ śrotriyāgārādvāhāryo 'nyatarasya caitadaharupavāsaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Here may <s>Pūṣan</s>, rich in a thousand gifts, sit down." Then he has her sacrifice with an <s>Agni</s>-cooked mess. Then, having taken a portion from this cooked mess and sprinkled it with ghee, he offers: "To <s>Agni</s>, svāhā. To <s>Agni</s> possessed of fire, svāhā. To <s>Agni</s> the eater of food, svāhā. To <s>Agni</s> <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s>, svāhā." As long as he lives he tends this fire with rice or barley in the evening and morning. In the evening he offers the first oblation, "To <s>Agni</s>, svāhā," and the second, "To <s>Prajāpati</s>, svāhā." Some recite that in the morning the solar oblation is first. The <s>aupāsana</s> fire must be maintained constantly; if it has gone out, it is to be churned anew, or brought from the house of a learned Brahmin. On that day one or the other of them fasts.

children.text: aṣṭamyaḥ parvāṇi copavasatyāgneyena sthālīpākena parvasu yajate vāgyata āsta ā nakṣatrāṇāmudayāduditeṣu nakṣatreṣu vatsamanvārabhyotthāpayatyudāyuṣā svāyuṣetyathaināṃ dhruvamarundhatīmanyāni ca nakṣatrāṇyabhivīkṣayati namo brahmaṇe dhruvāyācyutāyāstvityetenānuvākena dhruvamupatiṣṭhate dhruvakṣitirdhruvayonirdhruvamasi dhruvata sthitam
children.translated_text: On the eighth lunar day and on the parvan days he fasts, or he sacrifices on the parvan days with a rice-dish for <s>Agni</s>. He remains restrained in speech until the rising of the nakṣatras. When the nakṣatras have risen, he touches the calf and raises her up with, "Rise up with life, with your own life." Then he makes her look at <s>Dhruva</s>, <s>Arundhatī</s>, and the other nakṣatras. With the section beginning, "Homage to <s>Brahman</s>; may you be firm, unfailing," he worships <s>Dhruva</s>: "You are of firm dwelling, of firm womb; you are firm, established in firmness."

children.text: tvaṃ nakṣatrāṇāṃ methyasi sa mā pāhi pṛtanyata iti saptarṣayaḥ prathamāṃ kṛttikānāmarundhatīṃ dhruvatāṃ ye ha ninyuḥ
children.translated_text: "You are the peg among the nakṣatras; protect me from hostile attack." The Seven Seers are those who led <s>Arundhatī</s>, first among the <s>Kṛttikās</s>, to firmness.

children.text: ṣaṭkṛttikā mukhyayogaṃ vahantīyamasmākaṃ bhrājatvaṣṭamītyarundhatīṃ trirātramakṣāralavaṇāśināvadhaḥśāyinau brahmacāriṇau bhavato 'tha caturthyāmapararātre 'ntarāgāre 'gnimupasamādhāya jayābhyātānānrāṣṭrabhṛta iti hutvaitā āhutīrjuhotyagne prāyaścitte tvaṃ devānāṃ prāyaścittirasi brāhmaṇāstvā nāthakāmaḥ prapadye
children.translated_text: "The six <s>Kṛttikās</s>, bearing the chief conjunction, may this eighth night shine for us." Having shown <s>Arundhatī</s>, for three nights the two eat no alkaline or salty food, sleep on the ground, and observe chastity. Then, in the latter part of the fourth night, after setting the fire in order inside the house and offering the <s>Jayā</s>, <s>Abhyātāna</s>, and <s>Rāṣṭrabhṛt</s> oblations, he offers these oblations: "O <s>Agni</s> of expiation, you are the expiation among the gods. As a brāhmaṇa desiring protection, I resort to you."

children.text: yāsyāṃ patighnī tanūḥ prajāghnī paśughnī lakṣmighnī jāraghnīmasyai tāṃ kṛṇomi svāhā
children.translated_text: "Whatever body of hers is husband-killing, offspring-killing, cattle-killing, prosperity-killing, or lover-killing, that body of hers I make away with. Svāhā."

children.text: vāyo prāyaścitta āditya prāyaścitte prajāpate prāyaścitte tvaṃ devānāṃ prāyaścittirasi brāhmaṇastvā nāthakāmaḥ prapadye
children.translated_text: "O <s>Vāyu</s> of expiation, O <s>Āditya</s> of expiation, O <s>Prajāpati</s> of expiation, you are the expiation among the gods. As a brāhmaṇa desiring protection, I resort to you."

children.text: yāsyai ninditā tanūstāmito nāśayāmasi svāheti ||
children.translated_text: "That censured body of hers: from here we destroy it. Svāhā."

children.text: athaināṃ tūṣṇīṃ hiṃkṛtya vāgyata upetyāmūhamasmi sā tvaṃ dyaurahaṃ pṛthivī tvaṃ sāmāhamṛktvaṃ tāvehi saṃbhavāva saha reto dadhāvahai puṃse putrāya vettavai rāyaspoṣāya suprajāstvāya suvīryāyetyathāsyā apavṛttārtho 'pavṛttārthāyai mukhena mukhaṃ saṃnidhāya prāṇityetaṃ prāṇamapānihīti taṃ sā pratyapānityathāsyā ācāntodakāyai pāṇī prakṣālyābhimṛśati karaddadhacchivena tvā pañcaśākhena hastenāvidviṣāvatā sāhasreṇa yaśasvinābhimṛśāmi suprajāstvāyeti bhasaddeśaṃ yadā malavadvāsā syādathaināṃ brāhmaṇapratiṣiddhāni vratāni saṃśāsti yāṃ malavadvāsasamiti caturthyāṃ snātāṃ prayatavastrāṃ brāhmaṇasaṃbhāṣāṃ saṃ te manasā mana ityetenānuvākenopasaṃviśati sarvāṇyupāyanāni mantravanti bhavantītyāśmarathyo yaccādau yaccartāvityālekhanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, after humming over her silently, he approaches her restrained in speech: "I am that; you are she. You are heaven; I am earth. You are the <s>Sāman</s>; I am the <s>Ṛc</s>. Come, let the two of us unite; together let us place seed, for obtaining a male son, for increase of wealth, for good offspring, and for heroic strength." Then, when his purpose with her has been accomplished, he brings his mouth close to the mouth of her whose purpose has been accomplished and breathes: "I breathe this breath into you." She breathes that back. Then, when she has sipped water, he washes his hands and touches her with, "With my hand, five-branched, bringing, holding, auspicious, free from hostility, thousandfold and glorious, I touch you for good offspring," at the region of the buttocks, when she is wearing a garment stained with menses. Then he instructs her in the observances forbidden by brāhmaṇas, saying, "The woman who wears a stained garment." On the fourth day, when she has bathed, wears clean garments, and may converse with brāhmaṇas, he lies with her using the section beginning, "Together with your mind, my mind." According to <s>Āśmarathya</s>, all approaches are accompanied by mantras; according to <s>Ālekhana</s>, both the first approach and the approach in the season are so.

children.text: athāsyāḥ prathamagarbhiṇyāścaturthe māsi sīmantaṃ kurvantyāpūryamāṇapakṣe puṇye nakṣatre payasi sthālīpākaṃ śrapayitvāntarāgāre 'gnimupasamādhāya jayābhyātānānrāṣṭrabhṛta iti hutvaitā āhutīrjuhoti bhūrbhuvaḥ suvaḥ prajāpata iti catasrastreṇyā śalalyā trīṇi darbhapuñjīlāni śalālugrapsamityupaniyamyordhvaṃ sīmantamunnayati bhūrbhuvaḥ suvo rākāmahaṃ yāste rāke
children.translated_text: Then, in the fourth month of her first pregnancy, they perform the sīmanta, the parting of the hair, in the waxing fortnight under an auspicious nakṣatra. Having cooked a rice-dish in milk, set the fire in order inside the house, and offered the <s>Jayā</s>, <s>Abhyātāna</s>, and <s>Rāṣṭrabhṛt</s> oblations, he offers these oblations: the four beginning "Bhūr, bhuvaḥ, suvaḥ; O <s>Prajāpati</s>." With a porcupine quill, three bunches of darbha grass, and the formula "śalālugrapsa," he fastens the hair and parts the sīmanta upward with, "Bhūr, bhuvaḥ, suvaḥ. I invoke <s>Rākā</s>; whatever is yours, O <s>Rākā</s>."

children.text: soma eva no rājetyāhurbrāhmaṇīḥ prajāḥ
children.translated_text: "They say that <s>Soma</s> alone is our king, and that the subjects are brāhmaṇical."

children.text: vivṛttacakrā āsīnāstīreṇa yamune taveti tīreṇāsau taveti vā yasyāstīre vasati purastādagneretāni nidhāya trīnodanānuddhṛtya sarpiṣopasicyopanidadhātyudaśarāvaṃ caturthaṃ teṣāmekaikamavekṣamāṇāṃ pṛcchati kiṃ paśyasīti putrāṃśca paśūṃśceti pratyāha teṣāmekaṃ brāhmaṇānbhojayedekaṃ brāhmaṇīrekaṃ saha kumāraiḥ sā prāśnāti vāgyata āsta ā nakṣatrāṇāmudayāduditeṣu nakṣatreṣviti samānam ||
children.translated_text: "Sitting with turned wheels by your bank, O <s>Yamunā</s>"; or, "By your bank, O so-and-so," naming the river on whose bank she lives. Having placed these things east of the fire, he takes up three portions of rice, sprinkles them with ghee, and sets them down, with a fourth bowl of water. As she looks at each of them, he asks, "What do you see?" She replies, "Sons and cattle." Of those portions, he should feed one to brāhmaṇas, one to brāhmaṇa women, and one she eats together with boys. She remains restrained in speech until the rising of the nakṣatras. When the nakṣatras have risen, the rest is the same as before.

children.text: atha puṃsavanaṃ tṛtīye māsi caturthādau vā tiṣyeṇa vā hastena vānurādhairvottarairvā proṣṭhapadairnyagrodhāvarodhamāhṛtyānavasnātayā kumāryā dṛṣatputre dṛṣatputreṇa peṣayitvāntarāgāre 'gnimupasamādhāya jayābhyātānānrāṣṭrabhṛta iti hutvaitā āhutīrjuhoti yastvā hṛdā kiriṇeti catasro 'pareṇāgniṃ prācīmuttānāṃ nipātyāthāsyā dakṣiṇe nāsikāchidre 'ṅguṣṭhenānunayati puṃsavanamasyamuṣyā iti sā hetyāha pumāṃsameva janayatyatha kṣipraṃsuvanaṃ yajñopavītaṃ kṛtvāpa ācamyānāprītena śarāveṇānusrotasamudakamāhṛtya pattastūryantīṃ nidhāya mūrdhañchoṣyantīmabhimṛśati daśabhistvāṅgulibhirabhimṛśāmi daśamāsyāya sūtavā ityathainām adbhir avokṣati yathaiva vātaḥ pavate yathā samudra ejati
children.translated_text: Then the puṃsavana is performed in the third month, or at the beginning of the fourth, under <s>Tiṣya</s>, <s>Hasta</s>, the <s>Anurādhās</s>, or the later <s>Proṣṭhapadas</s>. Having brought a shoot from the hanging root of a banyan tree and had it ground on a grinding-stone by an unbathed maiden with another grinding-stone, he sets the fire in order inside the house and offers the <s>Jayā</s>, <s>Abhyātāna</s>, and <s>Rāṣṭrabhṛt</s> oblations. He offers these oblations, the four beginning, "You whom I scatter with the heart." To the west of the fire he lays her down facing east, on her back; then he pours the preparation with his thumb into her right nostril, saying, "This is puṃsavana for so-and-so's wife." She says, "Yes." Thus he causes a male child to be born. Then he performs the quick-birth rite: having put on the sacred thread, sipped water, and brought water downstream in an unfired bowl, he places the woman who is about to give birth lying on the bed and touches her head, which is becoming dry, with, "With ten fingers I touch you for giving birth in the tenth month." Then he sprinkles her with water: "Just as the wind blows, just as the ocean stirs,"

children.text: evaṃ kumāra ejatu saha jarāyuṇāvapadyatāmityatha yadyaparā na patetpāṇinodakamādāya mūrdhanyenāmavasiñcettilade 'vapadyasva na māṃsamasi no dalamavapadyasvāsāviti yadi garbhaḥ sraṃsed ārdreṇa pāṇinā trir ūrdhvaṃ nābher unmṛjet parāñcaṃ tvā nārvāñcaṃ tvaṣṭā badhnātu bandhanaiḥ
children.translated_text: "so may the child stir; may it come forth together with the placenta." Then, if the afterbirth does not fall, he takes water in his hand and pours it over her head: "O sesame-like one, fall down; you are not flesh, nor a piece of flesh. Fall down, O so-and-so." If the embryo slips, with a wet hand he should wipe upward three times above the navel: "May <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s> bind you with bonds, not turned away, not turned hither."

children.text: sa ṛtūnupaśeṣva daśamāso 'vīraheti ||
children.translated_text: He should attend to her seasons: “may there be a ten-month child, free from loss of the male,” thus.

children.text: vijātāyāḥ paridāṃ karoti dakṣiṇārdhe 'gārasyāgnimupasamādhāya sarṣapānphalīkaraṇamiśrānañjalāvadhyupya juhoti śaṇḍo marka upavīrastuṇḍikera ulūkhalaḥ
children.translated_text: When she has given birth, he performs the protective enclosure: having placed the fire in the southern half of the house, he pours mustard seeds mixed with chaff into his joined hands and offers them: “<s>Śaṇḍa</s>, <s>Marka</s>, <s>Upavīra</s>, <s>Tuṇḍikera</s>, <s>Ulūkhala</s>,

children.text: cyavano naśyatāditaḥ svāhetyevaṃ dvitīyāmevaṃ tṛtīyāmathāparāṃ keśinī śvalominī khajābojopakāśinī
children.translated_text: <s>Cyavana</s>, perish from here; svāhā.” In the same way a second time, and in the same way a third time. Then another: “The hairy one, the dog-haired one, the lame one, the seed-exposing one,

children.text: apeta naśyatāditaḥ svāhetyevaṃ dvitīyāmevaṃ tṛtīyāmathāparāmaryamṇaḥ kumbhīpātraḥ pātrapāṇirnipuṇiḥ
children.translated_text: go away, perish from here; svāhā.” In the same way a second time, and in the same way a third time. Then another: “<s>Aryaman</s>’s pot-vessel, vessel-handed, skillful one,

children.text: apeta naśyatāditaḥ svāhetyevaṃ dvitīyāmevaṃ tṛtīyāmathāparāṃ miśravāsasaḥ kauberakā rakṣorājena preṣitāḥ
children.translated_text: go away, perish from here; svāhā.” In the same way a second time, and in the same way a third time. Then another: “Those of mixed garments, the <s>Kauberaka</s> beings, sent by the king of the rakṣases,

children.text: grāmaṃ sajānayo gacchantīcchanto 'paridākṛtānsvāhā
children.translated_text: go with their kinswomen to the village, desiring those for whom the protective enclosure has not been made; svāhā.

children.text: etānghnataitāngṛhṇītetyayaṃ brāhmaṇo dūtaḥ
children.translated_text: Strike them; seize them. This brāhmaṇa is the messenger.

children.text: tānagniḥ paryasarattānindrastānbṛhaspatiḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Agni</s> has surrounded them, <s>Indra</s> has surrounded them, <s>Bṛhaspati</s> has surrounded them.

children.text: tānahaṃ veda brāhmaṇaḥ pramṛśataḥ kūṭadantānvikeśānlambanastanānsvāhā
children.translated_text: I, the brāhmaṇa, know those who touch: with pointed teeth, disheveled hair, and hanging breasts; svāhā.

children.text: naktaṃcāriṇa uraspeśāñchūlahastānkapālapān
children.translated_text: Night-wanderers, chest-striped, holding spears, drinking from skulls,

children.text: pūrva eṣāṃ pitaityuccaiḥ śrāvyakarṇakaḥ
children.translated_text: the father of these goes first, with ears that hear loudly.

children.text: mātā jaghanyā sarpati grāme vidhuramicchantī svāhā
children.translated_text: The mother creeps behind, seeking a widower in the village; svāhā.

children.text: pradoṣacāriṇī svasā saṃdhinā prekṣate kulam
children.translated_text: The sister, wandering at dusk, looks upon the household through the junction.

children.text: yā svapantaṃ bodhayati yasyai vijātāyāṃ manaḥ
children.translated_text: She who wakes the sleeping man, she whose mind is upon the woman who has given birth:

children.text: tāsāṃ tvaṃ kṛṣṇavartmane klomānaṃ hṛdayaṃ yakṛt
children.translated_text: their lungs, heart, and liver, O you of the black path,

children.translated_text: O <s>Agni</s>, burn out their eyes; svāhā.” In exactly the same way he does this as she goes out and as she enters, casting down day by day until the tenth day.

children.translated_text: If she gives birth to a male child, he touches him, saying, “Grow.” Wrapping a middle leaf of palāśa around him, with it he murmurs into his right ear, “I place <s>bhūḥ</s> in you,” into the left, “I place <s>bhuvaḥ</s> in you,” and into the right, “I place <s>suvaḥ</s> in you”; or else into the left twice and into the right only once. Then he addresses him: “Be a stone; be an axe; be unwounded gold.

children.text: vedo vai putranāmāsi sa jīva śaradaḥ śatam
children.translated_text: You are indeed named <s>Veda</s>, O son; live a hundred autumns.

children.text: medhāṃ te devaḥ savitā medhāṃ devī sarasvatī
children.translated_text: May the god <s>Savitṛ</s> place intelligence in you; may the goddess <s>Sarasvatī</s> place intelligence in you.

children.text: medhāṃ te aśvināvubhāvādhattāṃ puṣkarasrajau
children.translated_text: May both <s>Aśvins</s>, lotus-garlanded, place intelligence in you.

children.text: vedo vai putranāmāsi sa jīva śaradaḥ śatamityathainaṃ dadhi madhu ghṛtamiti saṃsṛjya tribhirdarbhapuñjīlairhiraṇyena vā triḥ prāśayatyapāṃ tvauṣadhīnāṃ rasaṃ prāśayāmyāyurvarco yaśo medhāṃ tvayi dadhāmi savitrā prasūtastvaṣṭā vīramadhātsa me śatāyuredhi bhūrbhuvaḥ suvarityathāsya dakṣiṇena hastena dakṣiṇaṃ hastamabhīvāṅguṣṭhamabhīva lomāni gṛhṇātyagnirāyuṣmānityetairmantrairnavanītena pāṇī abhyajya hiraṇyaṃ haste kṛtvā ||
children.translated_text: You are indeed named <s>Veda</s>, O son; live a hundred autumns.” Then, having mixed curds, honey, and ghee, he makes him taste it three times with three bunches of darbha grass, or with gold: “I make you taste the essence of waters and plants. I place life, radiance, fame, and intelligence in you. Impelled by <s>Savitṛ</s>, <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s> has set a hero; become one with a hundred-year life for me. <s>Bhūḥ</s>, <s>bhuvaḥ</s>, <s>suvaḥ</s>.” Then with his right hand he grasps the child’s right hand, including the thumb and the hairs, after anointing the hands with fresh butter and placing gold in the hand, with the mantras beginning “<s>Agni</s> is long-lived.”

children.text: agnau pratāpyābhimṛśatyagnestvā tejasā sūryasya varcasendrasyendriyeṇa viśveṣāṃ tvā devānāṃ kratunābhimṛśāmi
children.translated_text: Having heated it at the fire, he touches him: “With <s>Agni</s>’s heat, with the sun’s radiance, with <s>Indra</s>’s power, with the resolve of all the gods, I touch you.”

children.text: aṅgādaṅgātsaṃbhavasi hṛdayādadhi jāyase
children.translated_text: From limb after limb you arise; from the heart you are born.

children.text: ātmā vai putranāmāsi sa jīva śaradaḥ śatamityathainaṃ vātsapreṇābhimṛśati divasparītyanuvākena yatra śete tadabhimṛśati veda te bhūmi hṛdayaṃ divi candramasi śritam
children.translated_text: You are indeed named self, O son; live a hundred autumns.” Then he touches him with the <s>Vātsapra</s> hymn, with the section beginning “from heaven.” He touches the place where he lies: “I know your heart, O earth, lodged in heaven, in the moon.

children.text: vedāmṛtasya goptāraṃ māhaṃ pautramaghaṃ rudamityathainaṃ māturupastha ādadhāti mā te putraṃ rakṣo vadhīnmā dhenuratyāsāriṇī
children.translated_text: I know the guardian of immortality; may I not weep over misfortune involving a grandson.” Then he places him in the mother’s lap: “May no rakṣas slay your son; may no over-running cow harm him.

children.text: priyā dhanasya bhūyā edhamānā sve vaśa iti stanaṃ pratidhāpayatyayaṃ kumāro jarāṃ dhayatu dīrghamāyuḥ
children.translated_text: May you become dear to wealth, increasing under your own power.” He makes him take the breast: “May this boy suck old age and long life.

children.text: tasmai tvaṃ stana prapyāyāyurvarco yaśo balamiti saṃviṣṭābhyāṃ paridāṃ karoti nāmayati na rudati yatra vayaṃ vadāmasi yatra cābhimṛśāmasīti śirasta udakumbhaṃ nidadhātyāpaḥ supteṣu jāgrata rakṣāṃsi nirito nudadhvamiti naitāsāmapāmudakārthaṃ kurvantyatha yadi ciraṃ na vijāyate srajamenāṃ darśayetparimuktāyāṃ kṣipramevopanirharedyadā yadā sūtikārogaḥ syāddakṣiṇasya padastaptodakena pārṣṇiṃ kledayitvā tadā tadā taṃ deśamavamārṣṭi yatrāsyā duḥkhaṃ bhavati dhanurmaṭacī puruṣasya hastayorekaśataṃ śṛṇoraṅga te dhāpayitārastvaṃ rogasyeśiṣe tvamu rogasya sūtikārogabhaiṣajyamasyamuṣyā iti ||
children.translated_text: For him, O breast, swell with life, radiance, fame, and strength.” For the two lying down he performs the protective enclosure: “It bows down; it does not cry where we speak and where we touch.” He places a water-jar by the head: “Waters, keep watch while they sleep; drive the rakṣases away from here.” They do not use these waters for ordinary water needs. Then, if she does not give birth for a long time, he should show her a garland, and when it has been loosened he should quickly carry it away. Whenever there is puerperal pain, after moistening the heel of her right foot with hot water, he wipes the place where her pain is: “<s>Dhanurmaṭacī</s>, one hundred in a man’s hands, hear, O limb: your nurses are many; you rule over the disease; you are the remedy for the disease, the medicine for puerperal pain, for this woman.”

children.text: upanirharanti sūtikāgnimaupāsanamatiharanti sa eṣa uttapanārtho bhavati nāsminkiṃ cana karma kriyate daśamyāṃ snātau mātāputrau śucyagāraṃ kurvantyupanirharantyaupāsanaṃ sūtikāgnimatiharantyantarāgāre 'gnimupasamādhāya jayābhyātānānrāṣṭrabhṛta iti hutvaitā āhutīrjuhoti dhātā dadātu no rayimityaṣṭau daśamyāṃ putrasya nāma dadhāti dvyakṣaraṃ caturakṣaraṃ vā ghoṣavadādyantarantasthaṃ dīrghābhiniṣṭānāntaṃ taddhi pratiṣṭhitamiti vijñāyate pitā mātetyagre 'bhivyāhareyātāṃ vijñāyate mama nāma prathamaṃ jātavedaḥ pitā mātā ca dadhaturyadagra iti dve nāmanī kuryādvijñāyate ca tasmāddvināmā brāhmaṇo 'rdhuka iti nakṣatranāma dvitīyaṃ syādanyataradguhyaṃ syādanyatareṇainamāmantrayeran ||
children.translated_text: They carry out the birth-room fire and bring in the <s>aupāsana</s> fire. This is for the purpose of warming; no rite at all is performed in it. On the tenth day, when the mother and son have bathed, they make a clean room; they carry out the <s>aupāsana</s> fire and bring in the birth-room fire. Having set the fire in order inside the house and offered the <s>Jayā</s>, <s>Abhyātāna</s>, and <s>Rāṣṭrabhṛt</s> oblations, he offers these oblations, the eight beginning, "May <s>Dhātṛ</s> give us wealth." On the tenth day he gives the son a name, of two syllables or of four syllables, beginning and ending with a voiced sound or a semivowel, and ending in a long vowel or in a visarga, for that is known to be well established. The father and mother should first pronounce it aloud; for it is known, "My first name, O <s>Jātavedas</s>, father and mother gave at the beginning." He should make two names; and it is known, "Therefore a brāhmaṇa with two names prospers." The second should be a nakṣatra-name. One of the two should be secret, and with the other they should address him.

children.text: viproṣya hariṇī dūrve ādāya gṛhānupodeti gṛhā mā bibhīta mā vepiḍhvamūrjaṃ bibhrata emasi
children.translated_text: Having been away, he takes green dūrvā grass and approaches the houses: "Houses, do not fear; do not tremble. Bearing nourishment, we have come.

children.text: ūrjaṃ bibhradvaḥ sumanāḥ suvarcā gṛhānemi manasā modamānaḥ
children.translated_text: Bearing nourishment, well-disposed and rich in radiance, I come to you, O houses, rejoicing in mind.

children.text: yeṣāṃ pravasannadhyeti yeṣu saumanaso bahuḥ
children.translated_text: Those in which one studies while away, those in which there is much good-mindedness,

children.text: gṛhānupahvayāmahe te no jānantu jānataḥ
children.translated_text: we call upon the houses; let them know us as people who know them.

children.text: ime gṛhāḥ prati jīveṣvasthurūrjaṃ bibhrato jagataḥ suśevāḥ
children.translated_text: These houses have stood firm among living beings, bearing nourishment, moving, and kindly.

children.text: eha vatsaḥ krandatvā kumāra ā dhenavo bahulā nityavatsāḥ
children.translated_text: Here let the calf cry out, the boy; let the milch cows be many, always with calves.

children.text: upahūtaṃ goaśvamupahūtā ajāvayaḥ
children.translated_text: Cattle and horses have been summoned; goats and sheep have been summoned;

children.text: atho annasya kīlāla upahūto gṛheṣu me
children.translated_text: and the cream of food has been summoned here in my houses.

children.text: ūrjaṃ bibhrata emasyūrjā vaḥ saṃsṛjāmi ramadhvaṃ mā bibhītaneti tṛṇe prāsyati śivā upamitaḥ pramitaśca santviti dvārye saṃmṛśati kṣemāya vaḥ śivaḥ śāntyai prapadya iti prapadyate dakṣiṇapūrvābhyāmanuvīkṣate 'bhayaṃ vo 'stvabhayaṃ me astviti bhāryāṃ saṃgacchamnānāmanumantrayate viśvā uta tvayā vayamityetayā putraṃ saṃgacchamānamanumantrayate 'ṅgādaṅgātsaṃbhavasīti dvābhyāmathainaṃ mūrdhaṃstriravajighretpaśūnāṃ tvā hiṃkāreṇābhijighrāmi prajāpataye tvā hiṃkāreṇābhijighrāmi prajāpatista āyurdadhātu sa me śatāyuredhi bhūrbhuvaḥ suvariti sarvebhyaḥ prāṇebhyo jātāsi sā jīva śaradaḥ śatamiti duhiturathainaṃ ṣaṣṭhe māsyannaṃ prāśayati tasya sa eva prāśanakalpo yo medhājanana etāvannānā bhūrityagre prāśayati bhuva iti dvitīyaṃ suvariti tṛtīyam ||
children.translated_text: "Bearing nourishment we have come; with nourishment I unite you. Take delight; do not fear." Thus he casts the grasses down. Saying, "May what is measured and what is set out be auspicious," he touches the two doorposts. Saying, "For your security, for auspiciousness, for peace I enter," he enters. He looks toward the southeast: "May there be fearlessness for you; may there be fearlessness for me." He addresses his wife as he meets her, with the verse beginning, "All of us, together with you." He addresses the son as he meets him, with the two verses beginning, "From limb after limb you arise." Then he should smell him three times on the head: "With the hiṃkāra of cattle I smell you; for <s>Prajāpati</s> I smell you with the hiṃkāra. May <s>Prajāpati</s> place life in you. Become one who has a hundred-year life for me. <s>Bhūḥ</s>, <s>bhuvaḥ</s>, <s>suvaḥ</s>." For a daughter: "From all the breaths you have been born; live a hundred autumns." Then, in the sixth month, he makes him eat food. Its feeding procedure is the same as that for the production of intelligence, except this much is different: he first feeds him with "bhūḥ," a second time with "bhuvaḥ," and a third time with "suvaḥ."

children.text: athāsya sāṃvatsarikasya cauḍaṃ kurvanti yatharṣi yathopajñaṃ vā vijñāyate ca yatra bāṇāḥ saṃpatanti kumārā viśikhā iveti bahuśikhā ivetyathānnaṃ saṃskṛtya brāhmaṇānbhojayitvāśiṣo vācayitvāntarāgāre 'gnimupasamādhāya jayābhyātānānrāṣṭrabhṛta iti hutvaitā āhutīrjuhoti pūrṇā paścādimaṃ me varuṇa tattvā yāmi tvaṃ no agne sa tvaṃ no agne tvamagne 'yāsyanabhiśastīśca yadasya karmaṇo 'tyarīricaṃ prajāpata ityuttamāṃ hutvā gurave varaṃ dadātyapareṇāgniṃ gomayapiṇḍaṃ sarvabījānītyupaniyamya sarvabījānāmagraṃ gomayapiṇḍe nyupya śītoṣṇā apaḥ samānīya tābhirasya dakṣiṇaṃ godānamunattyāpa undantu jīvase dīrghāyutvāya varcasa iti treṇyā śalalyā vinīya trīṇi darbhapuñjīlānyūrdhvāgrāṇyupaniyacchatyoṣadhe trāyasvainaṃ svadhite mainaṃ hiṃsīriti lohitāyasaṃ kṣuraṃ tiryañcaṃ nidhāya pravapati yadṛṣīṇāṃ tryāyuṣaṃ jamadagneḥ kaśyapasya tryāyuṣam
children.translated_text: Then, when he is one year old, they perform his cūḍā, according to the seer or according to family tradition. And it is known, "Where the reeds come together, the boys are as if with arrows," or, "as if with many topknots." Then, having prepared food, fed brāhmaṇas, and had blessings spoken, he sets the fire in order inside the house. Having offered the <s>Jayā</s>, <s>Abhyātāna</s>, and <s>Rāṣṭrabhṛt</s> oblations, he offers these oblations: "Full behind," "This one of mine, O <s>Varuṇa</s>," "That truth of yours," "I come to you," "You, O <s>Agni</s>, are ours," "You, O <s>Agni</s>," "You, O <s>Agni</s>, who go," "and the revilings," and "whatever has exceeded this rite"; having offered the final oblation to <s>Prajāpati</s>, he gives a gift to the teacher. Behind the fire he sets down a lump of cow dung and all kinds of seed. Having cast the tips of all the seeds into the lump of cow dung, and having mixed cold and hot waters, with them he moistens the boy's right side-lock: "May the waters moisten you for life, for long life and radiance." Having separated it with three-pointed śalalī wood, he sets in place three bunches of darbha grass with their tips upward: "O plant, protect him. O razor, do not injure him." Having placed a red-metal razor crosswise, he shaves him: "The threefold life of the seers, the threefold life of <s>Jamadagni</s>, of <s>Kaśyapa</s>,

children.text: yaddevānāṃ tryāyuṣaṃ tanme 'stu tryāyuṣam
children.translated_text: "the threefold life that belongs to the gods: may that threefold life be mine."

children.text: yena pūṣā bṛhaspateragnerindrasya cāyuṣe 'vapattena te vapāmyasau dīrghāyutvāya varcasa ityevamevottaraṃ godānaṃ vāpayate keśānvāpayitvā gomayapiṇḍe nidadhātyathainaṃ gomayapiṇḍaṃ goṣṭha udakānta udumbaramūle darbhastambe vā nidadhātyathainaṃ snātamalaṃkurvanti ||
children.translated_text: "With that by which <s>Pūṣan</s> shaved for the life of <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, <s>Agni</s>, and <s>Indra</s>, with that I shave you, so-and-so, for long life and radiance." In just the same way he has the northern side-lock shaved. Having shaved the hairs, he places them in the lump of cow dung. Then he deposits that lump of cow dung in a cow-pen, at the edge of water, at the root of an udumbara tree, or in a clump of darbha grass. Then they bathe him and adorn him.
